newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN REDUCED LIQUIDITY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN REDUCED LIQUIDITY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed on Wednesday, with dealers predicting they would edge up during the rest of the week on reduced liquidity.
"It looks like the level of liquidity has come off and we're not expecting any treasury bill maturities today so we might see rates firming a bit," a market dealer said.

He said discount houses were selling treasury bills unchanged at 17.85 percent but bankers acceptances were being bought and sold at 18.75 and 18.50 percent hardening from 18.50 and 17.85 percent respectively.
Negotiable certificates of deposit were indicated softer at 19 percent (buying) from Tuesday's 20.50 and at 18.75 percent (selling) from 19.50 percent while call money held steady at 18.50 percent.
The central Reserve Bank gave a pre-settlement surplus figure of Z$33 million, down from Z$336.8 million previously.
